title: Salubong sa Sandaan: Miriam College marks 100 years with day-to-midnight festivities
summary: The institution's centennial celebrations bridged generations, honoring its trailblazers and inspiring the bright potential of its students.

blocks.text: The institution's centennial celebrations bridged generations, honoring its trailblazers and inspiring the bright potential of its students.

items: Miriam College celebrated its centennial year with a festive event called Salubong sa Sandaan, which included a Marian procession, a Centennial Mass, and a film festival showcasing student and employee works.
The celebration continued with a Centennial Night at Fairmont Hotel, featuring alumni gatherings, a fashion show, and the launch of a coffee table book documenting the institution's 100-year legacy.

Miriam College (MC) ushered in its historic centennial year with Salubong sa Sandaan, a festive day-to-midnight event held on September 11 and extending into the early hours of September 12. The school community—comprising employees, students, and alumni—gathered at the Loyola Heights campus to mark this significant milestone and celebrate an institution whose century-long legacy is rooted in faith, education, service, and leadership.

blocks.caption: A TRADITION. The Cultural Classical Dance Club of Miriam College High School led the traditional Karakol to open the Marian Procession, leading to the Centennial Mass.

blocks.text: The celebration opened with the entire community praying the Holy Rosary in honor of Mother Mary, after whom the school was named. Miriam is the Aramaic name of Mother Mary. This was followed by the Karakol, a traditional Marian procession, and the celebration of the Centennial Mass officiated by Bishop Honesto Ontioco, D.D., of the Diocese of Cubao.

blocks.caption: ROOTED IN FAITH. Maryknoll Sisters in the Philippines and Miriam College’s past presidents Dr. Loreta N. Castro, Dr. Patricia B. Licuanan, and Amb. Laura Q. Del Rosario join the community during the celebratory mass.

blocks.text: The festivities continued throughout the evening with the screening of short films created by students and MC employees for the Miriam College Film Festival (MCFF). The program also featured the school’s homegrown talents from its three campuses—MC Loyola Heights, MC Nuvali, and MC Alviera.

blocks.caption: TO THE BEAT. Sole2Soul and Company of One, two of the College’s homegrown dance groups, brought rhythm and energy to the festivities.

blocks.text: A much-anticipated moment was the MCFF awarding ceremony led by Miriam College President Dr. Maria Regina Lizares and Human Resources Director Dr. Noel Racho.

blocks.caption: FIRST FILM FESTIVAL. The first Miriam College Film Festival (MCFF) themed Mga Kwento ng Isang Daan,features six original student and employee films inspired by the institution’s 100-year legacy.

blocks.text: The centennial celebration continued on September 12 as generations of Maryknoll and Miriam College alumni gathered at the Fairmont Hotel in Makati for the Centennial Night and the launch of the coffee table book, ‘The Legacy We Carry: 100 Years From Maryknoll to Miriam.’

blocks.caption: REUNITED. Maryknoll and Miriam College alumni honor fellow alumna and newly-conferred National Artist for Design, Maria Beatriz “Patis” Pamintuan Tesoro (center), during the Centennial Night celebrations at Fairmont Hotel in Makati.

HONORING THEIR ROOTS. Miriam College President Dr. Gina Lizares and Sr. Marvelous Misolas, M.M. (2nd and 3rd from right) join the Maryknoll-Miriam alumni at the Fairmont Hotel for the launch of the centennial book, ‘The Legacy We Carry: 100 Years from Maryknoll to Miriam.‘
BLUE AND GOLD. Miriam College’s official colors flooded the night from the vibrant hosts to the dynamic crowd.

blocks.text: The evening brought together alumni from across generations for a night of bonding, dancing, and music. A highlight of the celebration was a fashion show honoring alumni and newly conferred National Artist for Design Maria Beatriz “Patis” Pamintuan Tesoro.

blocks.caption: MC NUVALI REPRESENT! The campus’s Indayaw and Sikhayaw group wowed the community with their energetic moves.

blocks.text: From Maryknoll to Miriam, the institution’s influence on Philippine education—particularly women’s education—has become an enduring part of the nation’s history. From its beginnings in 1926 as a teacher-training school in Malabon–where it produced its first women graduates–the institution has gone on to nurture generations of students and distinguished alumni whose leadership and service have made a lasting impact across diverse fields, both in the Philippines and abroad. Today, Miriam College continues to expand its mission in education beyond the walls of its Loyola Heights campus with the opening of Miriam College Nuvali in 2014 and Miriam College Alviera in 2025.

blocks.caption: OVERFLOWING TALENT. Miriam College’s centennial celebration was held in the campus’ outdoor field from the morning of September 11 until midnight of September 12 to welcome another exciting century for the institution.
RYTHM AND ENERGY. Faculty and students in the crowd cheered for their favorite group performances throughout the night.

blocks.text: Miriam College’s year-long centennial celebration is expected to continue until September 2027, with a lineup of activities that will bring together the school community and its stakeholders. Among these are the Christmas Bazaar, a concert by the Miriam College Music Center, the MC100 Fun Run, and the Academic Conference on Teaching and Learning.
Learn more about Miriam College’s upcoming activities through its Instagram and Facebook pages. – Rappler.com
